name: Helix Biosystems LymphoDrain CX-3 Automated Lymphatic Assist Sleeve
product_name: Helix Biosystems LymphoDrain CX-3 Automated Lymphatic Assist Sleeve
description:
The LymphoDrain CX-3 is a semi-rigid wearable sleeve — available in full-arm, full-leg, and torso-panel configurations — that uses a network of micro-pneumatic chambers and piezoelectric compression nodes to mechanically stimulate lymphatic drainage in patients with compromised lymphatic function. Originally designed for long-term augmentation patients whose lymphatic vessels were disrupted during implant installation, the CX-3 mimics the natural peristaltic rhythm of healthy lymphatic tissue at programmable intervals, preventing the edema and immune-suppression cascade that frequently follows major cybernetic integration surgery.

The sleeve's inner lining incorporates a bioelectric feedback layer sourced from Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's flexible conductor technology, allowing it to detect subcutaneous fluid accumulation in real time and adjust compression sequencing accordingly. A companion application running on any Saltmarsh-compatible personal device displays lymphatic flow metrics and flags early signs of infection or implant-site rejection. Higher-tier versions include a pharmaceutical delivery reservoir that can inject micro-doses of anti-inflammatory compounds directly into lymphatic vessels during compression cycles, eliminating the need for systemic medication.

In clinical settings, the CX-3 is prescribed as a mandatory recovery device following any Tier 1 or Tier 2 augmentation procedure involving thoracic or limb implants. In the streets, it has found a second life as a performance device — long-haul courier workers and manual laborers in Palladian construction sites use unauthorized units to manage chronic limb swelling from repetitive strain, and combat-augmented mercenaries wear them during downtime to accelerate recovery from trauma edema. The street nickname 'Milker' is considered derogatory by long-term medical users but has been enthusiastically adopted by the merc community.

social_impact: The LymphoDrain CX-3 has become an unexpected class marker in GLMZ — Tier 1 and Tier 2 citizens wear sleek, skin-toned clinical models discreetly under clothing, while Tier 4 and 5 workers sport bulkier, visibly worn units in safety-orange and industrial grey, often patched with tape and jury-rigged power leads. The device's visibility has made lymphatic health a strangely public conversation, with compression sleeve check-ins becoming a common social ritual in lower-tier break rooms and merc safe houses — and the device's absence a tell that someone either can't afford post-aug care or obtained their implants through channels that didn't include follow-up.
story_hooks: A black-market CX-3 shipment has been intercepted by Kelpline Logistics enforcers — the sleeves contain hidden data storage nodes, and someone very powerful wants them back before they're inventoried
A Tier 5 construction worker is dying of undiagnosed lymphatic failure because their CX-3 knockoff was never calibrated — the player characters must find the distributor before more workers succumb

A high-ranking Helix Biosystems executive has been secretly funding a programme to embed surveillance hardware in the CX-3's bioelectric feedback layer, monitoring the health data of thousands of augmented citizens
Someone is using the CX-3's pharmaceutical reservoir to dose wearers with a slow-acting loyalty compound — the source is either a corporation, a cult, or something stranger
